body.x: At CES 2026, long lines formed in front of the LEION booth as visitors waited to experience the product. Scenes of attendees speaking different languages while wearing ‘LEION HEY2’ unfolded repeatedly. The moment subtitles appeared in front of their eyes, expressions shifted from surprise to genuine excitement. Language barriers seemed to dissolve in real time.

Dr. Fei Wu, Founder of LLVision, emphasized during the interview, “We did not create AR glasses with a translation feature added. From the beginning, we designed a professional AR translation device specifically for face-to-face multilingual communication.” It was not a matter of adding a function, but redefining the problem itself.

Traditional earbud-based translation devices and voice translation services deliver translated audio only after the speaker finishes. This inevitably creates a time gap. Waiting disrupts the flow of conversation. Dialogue becomes fragmented and mechanical.

HEY2 redefines real-time interpretation—not as something that is heard, but as something that operates directly within the user’s field of vision. Word-by-word subtitles appear as the speaker talks, forming progressively and completing as the sentence ends. Real-time interpretation, in LLVision’s view, should be presented to the eyes rather than the ears. This strategic belief forms the core philosophy behind HEY2.

body.x: “Engineering Uninterrupted Conversation”

The strongest reaction at CES was not about accuracy—it was about continuity. HEY2 does not wait until a sentence is fully completed to deliver translation. Subtitles generate in real time as speech unfolds, allowing users to grasp context before a sentence even finishes. Conversation does not stop.

This is enabled by a dual-eye optical display system and a head-up interaction structure. Subtitles remain within the user’s field of vision and can be adjusted in size and position. There is no need to look down at a smartphone or wait for audio translation through earbuds. Eye contact remains intact.

Another key differentiator is the “Free Talk” function. The other person does not need to wear the glasses. The wearer reads subtitles directly, while the conversation partner views translated content on a smartphone screen. Multilingual communication becomes possible with just one person wearing the device.

“Systems that require both people to wear equipment struggle to scale,” Dr. Wu noted. “The moment one person puts it on, they should be able to communicate with anyone. That’s what makes it a true communication tool.” HEY2 was not designed as a translation device—it was engineered as an environment where conversation never stops.

body.cap: Dr. Fei Wu (吴飞), founder of LLVision and a first-generation developer of AR translation glasses, is being interviewed at the CES 2026 booth. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: “A First-Generation Pioneer Opening the Era of AR Translation Glasses”

LLVision is a first-generation company that pioneered the AR subtitle glasses category. Dr. Wu commercialized real-time AR subtitle technology and introduced the first-generation product, ‘Leion Hey,’ establishing a new product category in the market.

Released in 2022, Leion Hey was recognized globally after winning the Global Innovation Top 10 Award at the UNESCO Netexplo Forum. The core philosophy was already present: placing AI within the user’s field of vision rather than confining it to a screen.

“We have been researching AR and real-time subtitle technology for over 10 years,” Dr. Wu explained. “HEY2 is not simply a new product. It is the result of accumulated first-generation experience, data, and user feedback.”
The “visual translation” strategy of HEY2 did not emerge overnight. It evolved from validated real-world use cases and practical refinements made through first-generation products.

body.cap: Internal structure display of ‘LEION HEY2.’ Key components—including the camera-free AR display module, microphones, and battery—are showcased in a disassembled form, offering a clear view of the physical AI architecture that enables real-time translation. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: "Focus on Trust: Removing the Camera, Concentrating on Translation"

AR glasses can include many features—cameras, spatial recognition, recording, media consumption, and more. HEY2 deliberately chose a different path. Its design began with one purpose: face-to-face multilingual communication.
HEY2 does not include a camera. External speakers are also excluded. The device focuses solely on voice-based real-time translation. This decision was made to minimize privacy concerns.

In environments such as trade shows or business meetings, camera-equipped glasses can cause discomfort. By removing the camera, HEY2 was designed to foster trust. All data processing operates on Microsoft Azure cloud infrastructure and complies with GDPR standards.
“We asked not what more we could add, but what we should remove to earn trust,” Dr. Wu said. “For AR glasses to enter everyday life, trust must come before technical specifications.”

body.x: "AI That Becomes the Eyes, Ears, and Voice — Launching First in Korea"

HEY2 supports more than 100 languages and dialects and enables up to three-language simultaneous interpretation in multilingual environments. Four microphones, 360-degree spatial voice recognition, a 60-degree forward speaker-focus algorithm, and neural network-based noise reduction ensure stable performance even in noisy environments like CES.

By touching the temple of the glasses, users can activate an AI Q&A assistant. Beyond translation, the device supports information search and summarization, demonstrating its potential as an expandable AR information platform rather than merely a translation tool.

LLVision selected Korea as its first official launch market. With a high level of technology adoption and a strong early-adopter base, Korea serves as a strategic testbed before global expansion. The company has already established a local office, with more than 200 pre-orders secured.

Dr. Wu concluded the interview by stating, “What we want to create is not a grand vision of the future, but an environment where people speaking different languages can communicate naturally. We aim to remove the need to consciously think about interpretation or wait for translation. Technology should quietly support human conversation—not stand in front of it.”
At CES 2026, HEY2 demonstrated not just features, but direction. AI is no longer confined to monitors. It is moving directly into the human field of vision.

Meanwhile, LLVision’s ‘Leion Hey2’ will be officially launched in Korea through AI Babylon, a domestic AI solutions company, via the crowdfunding platform Wadiz. The campaign opens on February 27, with early-bird pricing available for participants.
Shipping for backers will begin sequentially from March 11. Detailed information is available on the official Wadiz crowdfunding page.
